sentences.text: 2. Shri Bapugouda Siddappa, learned counsel for appellant submitted that appeal is by claimant challenging dismissal of claim petition against respondent no.2-insurer and enhancement of compensation.

It was submitted that on 03.04.2013 at about 8.00 p.m., when claimant was traveling in Autorickshaw bearing Reg.no.KA.28/5182 ('Auto no.1') along with family members, another auto bearing Reg.no.KA-28/A-8433 ('Auto no.2') driven by its driver in rash and negligent manner Smt. Neelamma vs Smt. Boramma And Ors on 14 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/59291977/
2 dashed against Auto no.1 causing accident.

entities.text: Neelamma vs Smt. Boramma And Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In said accident, claimant sustained grievous injuries.
Despite taking treatment she did not recover fully and sustained permanent disability.

Claiming compensation, she filed claim petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act against owner and insurer of Auto no.1 and also owner of Auto no.2.
4.
Despite service of notice, owner of Auto no.2 did not participate.
He was placed exparte.
Owner and insurer of Auto no.1 opposed claim petition on all counts.
Based on pleadings, tribunal framed issues and recorded evidence of claimant as PW.1 and Dr.S.S.Nagathan as PW.2 and got marked Ex.P1 to P12.
Respondents NC: 2023:KHC-K:7386 examined official of insurer as RW.1.
Ex . R1
to R4 were marked.
5. On consideration, tribunal held that as on date of accident, Auto no.1 was not covered by insurance and therefore insurer was not liable to pay compensation.
Though it assessed compensation of Rs.47,000/-, it held owner of Auto no.1 liable to pay same.
6. It was submitted that Ex.R2 and R3 proposal form and legal notice dated 08.05.2014 would indicate that insured had paid premium amount towards insurance coverage on 03.04.2013 at 1.30 pm.
However, Ex.R1- insurance policy was issued showing commencement of coverage from midnight of 04.04.2013 to midnight of 03.04.2014.
As accident occurred at 8.00 p.m. on 03.04.2013 i.e. after receipt of insurance premium, tribunal would not be justified in dismissing claim petition against insurer.
7. In alternative, a prayer was made for passing an order for 'pay and recover' against insurer.

Insofar as enhancement, learned counsel submitted that though claimant had stated that she was earning Rs.8,000/- from coolie work and sustained disability of 5% to 10% due to fracture of third metacarpal as per PW.2, tribunal did not award compensation towards future loss of income and loss of income during laid up period.
Even compensation awarded under other heads was contended to be inadequate and sought enhancement.
9. On other hand, Smt.Preeti Patil Melkundi, learned counsel for insurer sought to justify award.
It was submitted that Ex.R1 clearly mentioned that insurance coverage would commence from midnight of 04.04.2013 to midnight of 03.04.2014.
It was further submitted that even in Ex.R2-Proposal form, period of coverage was clearly mentioned as above.
As accident occurred prior to commencement of said period, dismissal of claim petition against insurer was fully justified.
10. Heard learned counsel, perused impugned judgment and award and record.

From above submission, since claimant is in appeal challenging dismissal of claim petition against insurer and for enhancement of compensation, points that arise for consideration are :

sentences.text: "Point no.(i): Whether dismissal of claim petition against insurer calls for interference?

Point no.(ii): Whether claimant is entitled for enhancement of compensation?"
Point no.(i):
12. On perusal of impugned award, dismissal of claim petition against insurer is on ground that accident in question occurred prior to assumption of risk by insurer under Ex.R1-insurance policy.

13. Only ground on which said finding is sought to be assailed is that insurer had accepted premium at 1.30 p.m., on 03.04.2013 and accident had occurred at 8.00 p.m., on same day and therefore insurer cannot escape from liability.

Alternatively an order for 'pay and recover' is NC:
2023:KHC-K:7386 sought to be passed against insurer.

Hon'ble Supreme Court in following cases,
New India Assurance Co. Ltd. V. Sita Bai, reported in (1999) 7 SCC 575; National Insurance Co. Ltd.

entities.text: New India Assurance Co. Ltd. V. Sita Bai, reported in (1999) 7 SCC 575
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: V. Jikubhai Nathuji Dabhi, reported in (1997) 1 SCC 66 and National Insurance Co. Ltd. V. Sobina Iakai reported in (2007) 7 SCC 786,

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd. V. Sobina Iakai reported in (2007) 7 SCC 786
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: has held that in order to curb this widespread mischief of getting insurance policies after accidents, it is absolutely imperative to clearly hold that effectiveness of insurance policy would start from time and date specifically incorporated in policy and not from an earlier point of time.
14. Above ratio being consistent and unequivocal, contention of claimant would have to yield to it.
Consequently, point no.(i) is answered in negative.

Point no.(ii):
15.
Though claimant stated that she was earning Rs.8,000/- as coolie same is not substantiated.
In absence, notional income of Rs.7,000/- adopted for NC: 2023:KHC-K:7386 settlement of cases before Lok Adalath has to be accepted.
From medical records, claimant has sustained fracture of third metacarpal of right hand which normally does not cause any permanent disability.

Therefore,
tribunal would be justified in denying compensation towards future loss of income.
As said fracture is non-grievous, award of Rs.25,000/- towards pain and suffering would be just and proper.

Likewise, award of Rs.2,000/- towards medical expenses against bills produced, Rs.10,000/-
towards attendant and other incidental expenses for indoor treatment period of four days and Rs.10,000/- towards loss of amenities cannot be stated to be grossly inadequate or unjustified.
Though above fracture would not result in disability, it would have prevented claimant from working until healing of fracture.
Considering said period as three months, compensation of Rs.21,000/- is awarded.
Point no.(ii) for consideration is answered partly in affirmative.

In view of above, following :
NC: 2023:KHC-K:7386 ORDER Appeal is allowed in part.
Claimant is held entitled for additional compensation of Rs.21,000/- apart from Rs.47,000/- already awarded by tribunal.
Same shall carry interest at rate of 6% per annum from date of claim petition till deposit.
